title: Structured logging: levels, fields, correlation ids and sampling

videos.script: A log line written for a person is a sentence. A log line written for a machine is a record, with fields. {{two}} This lesson is about writing the second kind, and why it matters at three in the morning. You take two thousand checkouts, logged both ways, and ask both files the same question. One needs a regular expression nobody wants to maintain. The other needs a field name. {{question}} Then the formatter the shop uses, line by line. Levels, and who decides which ones get written. The trace id in every line, and the lines that have none. {{formatter}} An exception that becomes seventeen separate records, and the same one as a single record. And the volume: over a thousand lines a minute from a shop at five requests a second, and what to do about it. {{volume}}
